title: Saarbrücken Airport - Wikipedia
content: # Saarbrücken Airport. | SCN is located in Saarland SCN  SCN  Location of the airport in South Saarland | |. | |  |  | | --- | --- | | Passengers | 300,034 Increase+99,7% | | Aircraft movements | 006,882 Increase+16,6% | | Cargo (metric tons) | 000,010 Decrease-36,3% | | |. **Saarbrücken Airport** (IATA: **SCN**, ICAO: **EDDR**), or *Flughafen Saarbrücken*  or *Ensheim Airport* in German, is a minor international airport in Saarbrücken, the capital of the German state of Saarland. The history of aviation in Saarbrücken, the capital of the German federal state Saarland, began on 17 September 1928 in the district of St. Arnual. In 1929, routes to Frankfurt and on to Berlin and Karlsruhe and then to Munich, Vienna and Budapest were opened. In 1972, Saarbrücken Airport became one of 17 airports in Germany to offer international flights. After Hapagfly left, Air Berlin opened routes from Saarbrücken to Palma de Mallorca and Berlin–Tegel Airport, but it ceased flying in 2017.
